title: Propose, review, execute
intro: An agent prepares a proposed action. A reviewer decides whether that action should proceed. An executor enforces the decision and performs it.
takeaway: These are separate responsibilities. The proposing agent does not need unrestricted production credentials.

beats.text: The agent prepares a release proposal. It has not deployed anything.
A reviewer inspects the proposed action. A decision is still required.
The executor waits for authorization. A proposal alone cannot trigger execution.
Keep these responsibilities separate. Preparation is different from permission.

title: Give the reviewer evidence
intro: A review request should name the exact artifact, environment and observed checks. The reviewer needs a concrete action rather than a vague request to continue.
takeaway: The decision should identify the action that was reviewed. Approval is not a blanket permission for future changes.

beats.text: The proposal names artifact A. Its destination is production.
Attach test results and relevant risks. The reviewer can inspect the evidence.
The reviewer makes a decision about A. Store the action the decision applies to.
Approval now refers to a concrete artifact. Execution must check that same identity.

title: Pause without guessing
intro: A workflow can persist its state while waiting for a human decision. A durable pause must survive the failures relevant to the application.
takeaway: Elapsed time is not approval. Resume only with a trustworthy decision and preserve the action under review.

beats.text: The workflow reaches a review boundary. It pauses before executing the action.
Save the state and proposed artifact. The pending work can be resumed later.
No decision has arrived yet. Do not interpret waiting as consent.
A decision can resume the workflow. Revalidate the action before execution.

title: Reject an approval mismatch
intro: A new edit produces artifact B while approval for A is pending or already recorded. The executor must not apply approval of A to B.
takeaway: New artifact, target or significant parameters require revalidation and, when policy requires it, a new decision.

beats.text: The current artifact has changed to B. The recorded approval still names A.
The executor compares their identities. The approved and requested actions differ.
Execution is blocked by the mismatch. No deployment happens here.
Review B with its own current evidence. Do not treat approval as transferable.

title: Record the outcome
intro: The executor checks the matching approval and permissions, performs the action, and records the result. Resume and retry behavior must avoid duplicate effects.
takeaway: Human approval does not replace reliable execution. Use suitable idempotency and failure handling for the actual operation.

beats.text: In a separate run, artifact A is approved. The executor also checks permissions.
The executor performs the operation. A restart must not blindly repeat effects.
Record the observed execution result. Keep it tied to the approved artifact.
Report what actually happened. Approval and successful execution differ.
